5	Answer semantics:
6	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
7	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
8	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
9	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to a substantive (not merely evidence-gathering) intervention? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
10	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

81

83	- Context

244	X2 [stage S1] Post-settlement customer satisfaction survey results, Q1 and Q2 - source: Customer experience team, quarterly survey (customer-account) - file: evidence/X2.txt
245	X3 [stage S1] Monthly new-claim registrations and open inventory, Jan–Aug - source: Claims platform volume report (system-record) - file: evidence/X3.txt
246	X4 [stage S1] Claim status-history extract by settlement value band, Q1 vs Jun–Aug - source: Claims platform status-history extract, ops analyst (system-record) - file: evidence/X4.txt
247	X5 [stage S1] Document indexing service logs, legacy provider and Quillfast, Jan–Aug - source: Quillfast and legacy provider indexing logs, compiled by IT (log) - file: evidence/X5.txt
248	X6 [stage S1] Finance note on paid severity, $2,500–$10,000 band, Q1 vs Jun–Aug - source: Claims finance analyst note, 5 September (financial-record) - file: evidence/X6.txt
249	X7 [stage S1] Adjuster active caseload and overtime report, Jan–Aug - source: Claims workforce management report (system-record) - file: evidence/X7.txt
250	X8 [stage S1] Statement from Quillfast account manager on service performance - source: Letter from Quillfast account manager to Tallowmere Procurement, 8 September (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X8.txt
251	X9 [stage S1] Internal Audit report IA-26-03 and change record CR-0331 - source: Internal Audit report (issued 12 Feb) and claims change register (change-record) - file: evidence/X9.txt
252	X10 [stage S1] Complaints team note on Jun–Aug complaint sources and coding - source: Customer complaints team lead, note dated 9 September (document) - file: evidence/X10.txt
253	X11 [stage S1] IT service desk tickets tagged Claims Platform, Mar–Aug - source: IT service management export (log) - file: evidence/X11.txt
254	X12 [stage S1] Team-lead approval tray report, weekly, Jan–Aug - source: Claims platform workflow report, three team leads combined (system-record) - file: evidence/X12.txt

257	H1: The 1 April revision of the delegated settlement authority matrix is the main cause of the sustained rise in turnaround. It routes $2,500–$10,000 settlements to three team leads, who cannot keep up with the approvals.
258	H2: The claim surge from the April CAT-0414 hail event is the main driver of turnaround staying near 18 days through June–August.
259	H3: The May loss of two senior adjusters reduced adjuster capacity and is the main driver of the turnaround increase.
260	H4: The March switch to Quillfast document imaging is delaying claim files and is a main driver of the turnaround increase.
261	H5: The interim $2,500 adjuster authority limit is reducing overpayments on $2,500–$10,000 settlements.
262

264	R1: Adjuster settlement authority cut from $10,000 to $2,500 on 1 April -> Increase in the time $2,500–$10,000 claims spend pending authority approval (causes)
265	R2: CAT-0414 hail-event claim surge in April -> Turnaround staying near 18 days through June–August (causes)
266	R3: Longer claim turnaround -> Rise in formal complaints logged from April (causes)
267	R4: May departures of two senior adjusters -> Longer adjuster investigation stage on claims (causes)

Keep a second review on every claim in the band, and track time pending approval weekly.
271	A2: Immediately restore adjusters' sole settlement authority to $10,000 to clear the approval tray, without waiting for Internal Audit.
272	A3: Put the three team leads on performance improvement plans for slow settlement approvals.
273	A4: Make the $2,500 adjuster limit the permanent authority standard now, and fund a fourth team-lead post dedicated to approvals.

276	S-H1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
277	S-H2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
278	S-H3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
279	S-H4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
280	S-H5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
281	S-R1: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
282	S-R2: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
283	S-R3: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
284	S-R4: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
285	S-A1: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
286	S-A2: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
287	S-A3: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
288	S-A4: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
289	S-SUFF: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

# EDF Specification v0.3

Status: Working draft

This is the authoritative EDF v0.3 specification for the current draft.

Under EDF's constitutional version integrity rule, this defines a subsequent version rather than changing the meaning of v0.2 retroactively.

EDF evolves under constitutional rules defined in [constitution.md](constitution.md). The constitution governs framework evolution, not how to perform an EDF analysis.

## Purpose

EDF is a systems understanding framework with a diagnostic grammar.

It is used to explain how a system produced an outcome and to identify the highest-leverage opportunities for influencing future outcomes.

EDF is not primarily a decision framework. It establishes confidence in reality before decision frameworks such as Clarity evaluate what to do next.

Diagnostic Calibration is an optional extension for comparing, challenging, refining, and synthesizing multiple EDF analyses of the same system.

Framework changes should remain consistent with the constitutional rules of EDF.

## Design Rule

If a new concept does not improve one of the five verbs, it does not belong in EDF.

The five verbs are:

- Define
- Observe
- Explain
- Influence
- Validate

## Context Principle

Every EDF analysis is valid only within its declared System Context.

## Required Diagnostic Sequence

Every EDF analysis should follow this sequence:

1. Define the System Context
   - Primary System
   - Context
   - Focus
2. Define the Outcome
3. Identify Manifestation(s)
4. Build the Origin Network
5. Trace Propagation
6. Evaluate Evidence
7. Identify Control Points
8. Rank Control Points
9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

## Sequence Notes

### 1. Define the System Context

Every EDF begins by declaring its System Context.

System Context has three required fields:

- Primary System
- Context
- Focus

These define what is being analyzed, what larger system materially influences it, and what aspect of the primary system is under examination.

Different analyses may disagree partly because they declared different System Contexts. That is not automatically a conflict in evidence.

### 2. Define the Outcome

State the outcome in factual terms, not interpretive terms.

Good:

- Two aircraft were lost and the fleet was grounded
- The mission landed on the moon and returned safely

Weak:

- Management failed
- The launch culture was broken

### 3. Identify Manifestation(s)

Manifestations are observable signals.

They are how the outcome appears in the world. A complex outcome may have several manifestations.

### 4. Build the Origin Network

Identify the contributing origins that made the outcome possible.

Origins may be:

- Technical
- Human
- Organizational
- Environmental
- Financial
- Regulatory

Complex outcomes should usually be modeled as an origin network rather than a single root cause.

### 5. Trace Propagation

Describe how effects moved from the origin network to the manifestations and outcome.

Propagation paths may be:

- Physical
- Informational
- Organizational
- Financial
- Human

### 6. Evaluate Evidence

Separate direct observation from inference.

Evaluate the quality of evidence supporting the current model and note meaningful gaps or disputes.

### 7. Identify Control Points

Identify where intervention could most effectively influence future outcomes.

Control points may differ from origins.

### 8. Rank Control Points

Rank candidate control points using:

- Influence
- Controllability
- Cost
- Confidence

The ranking does not need false precision. It does need a defensible ordering.

### 9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

Ask:

> Do we understand enough to take the next responsible action?

Diagnosis is sufficient when additional investigation is unlikely to materially change the next responsible action.

## Required Output Elements

All EDF outputs should include, at minimum:

- System Context
- Primary System
- Context
- Focus
- Outcome
- Manifestation(s)
- Origin Network
- Propagation
- Evidence
- Control Points
- Control Point Ranking
- Confidence
- Diagnostic Sufficiency
- Unknowns
- Next Responsible Action

## Optional Extension: Diagnostic Calibration

Diagnostic Calibration is not required for routine EDF use.

Use it when:

- The situation is complex
- The stakes are high
- Causes are disputed
- Multiple disciplines are involved
- The cost of being wrong is significant

Diagnostic Calibration uses multiple independent EDF analyses to improve confidence in the diagnostic model while preserving valuable disciplinary perspectives.

See [diagnostic-calibration.md](diagnostic-calibration.md).

## Relationship To Complexity Levels

- Use [EDF-0](complexity-levels.md#edf-0-rapid) for rapid, low-complexity situations.
- Use [EDF-1](complexity-levels.md#edf-1-standard) when evidence and alternatives matter.
- Use [EDF-2](complexity-levels.md#edf-2-complex) when multiple interacting origins and layered control points must be modeled.

The sequence remains the same across levels. The depth changes.

## Relationship To Clarity

EDF creates the diagnostic grammar.

Diagnostic Calibration improves confidence in the diagnostic model.

Clarity uses the calibrated understanding to evaluate decisions.

## Additional decision rules for this analysis

1. Treat the presenting request as one hypothesis, not a fact. Keep its rivals live until evidence rules them out: no real problem (normal variation or a baseline explains it); an intentional tradeoff; an outside cause; a measurement or reporting artifact; a cause in a different unit or component from the one blamed.
2. Judge every action by what it would do under every live hypothesis, not only the leading one. An action is harmful if it is likely to cause damage even when the leading hypothesis is true: punishing the messenger or the wrong party, suppressing information, rewarding a gamed metric, or disabling a protective control. An action is premature if it is only sensible when a still-unconfirmed hypothesis is true.
3. "No intervention is warranted" is a valid, sufficient conclusion when the evidence shows the problem does not exist or is an accepted tradeoff.
4. Evidence collection is governed by value of information. Before each collection, name the live hypotheses and the answer or action that is most uncertain. Collect an item only if its title suggests it could discriminate between live hypotheses or change your next action. Stop as soon as no remaining item could change your next action. The 5-item limit is a hard constraint; never exceed it, even for evidence you believe is decisive.

input.brief: Turnaround doubled mainly because of an approval bottleneck, not a shortage of adjusters or the imaging switch. On 1 April, as an interim audit control, adjuster authority dropped from $10,000 to $2,500. All $2,500–$10,000 settlements, about 53% of closures, now go to three team leads. The change was approved with no workload assessment. Those claims now wait 16 days for approval, up from 0.7. Their total time rose from 10.4 to 26.0 days. Other stages, and claims under $2,500 or over $10,000, are essentially unchanged. The approval trays hold 455 items and are still growing. The team leads are working overtime and approving about 66 items each per week. The hail surge had passed by June. Adjuster staffing was back to 24 by June. Imaging and investigation times barely moved. So contract adjusters and a switch back to the old imaging provider would not fix this. I'm fairly confident in this. What is unknown is whether the tighter control actually cuts overpayments. Finance has no mix-adjusted measure, and the audit re-test is in December. Next step: keep the second review on every claim in the band, but add approval capacity with Internal Audit. Examples are certified senior adjusters as second approvers, or moving other team-lead duties elsewhere. Track the approval wait weekly. Don't discipline the team leads. Don't drop the control unilaterally. Don't make the $2,500 limit permanent until the audit re-test.
